newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-DAVIES MOVES INTO HALFWAY CONTENTION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DAVIES MOVES INTO HALFWAY CONTENTION.

text.p: Britain's Laura Davies, the biggest draw in the women's game, shot a four-under-par 68 to get back into contention in the WPGA Championship of Europe on Friday, then admitted some of the fun has gone out of golf for her this season.
Veteran compatriot Dale Reid, 38, compiled a flawless six-birdie 66 to lead by two shots from fellow-Scot Catriona Matthew, England's Lora Fairclough and Marie-Laure de Lorenzi of France.
Davies was in the next group a shot further back.
After an outstanding three seasons, in which she won 24 times worldwide, the 33 year-old Davies has dropped to number three in the world behind Sweden's Annika Sorenstam and Australian Karrie Webb.

Not that her form has been too dismal. She has won on both sides of the Atlantic - the Standard Register Ping Tournament on the LPGA circuit and the Danish Open in Europe - and she lies seventh on the U.S. money list with over 400,000 dollars.

"But it's not nearly so much fun when you're not in contention every week," she admitted. "I won nine times last year, and anything less is frustrating. I'm still playing well but my putting has not been so good, and so I'm not getting the results.
"But I know I just have to accept it. I've had more than my fair share of luck over the past three years, and it's bound to even out in the end."
Reid, who has not tasted victory since 1991, has sharpened her game by playing in the United States this year. "I know I can win again." she said.
